Summary.Name: DeepCORO-JEPA
Summary.Description: One EchoJEPA video encoder (ViT-L) that segments the coronary tree into 26 SYNTAX classes itself and, from up to 12 diagnostic coronary angiography runs per study, predicts for each coronary segment the % diameter stenosis, the probability of a significant lesion and the probabilities of calcification, thrombus and chronic total occlusion (CTO), plus LAD-territory FFR and iFR (value and probability of an abnormal result). Model v15 adds one probability per study for each of the three lesion findings and an estimate of the coronary dominance. 17 segments are supported: the posterior left ventricular branch (lvp) had no training target in v15, so its values are returned for compatibility but are not meaningful, never raise a flag and are never displayed. Each probability except the study-level lesion probabilities comes with a yes/no call at a threshold chosen on the validation set. The encoder runs at most twice per study: full views at 224 px, then up to 4 tracked 320 px crops per segment. No segmentation map has to be provided. Version 2.0.0 serves model v15. Earlier working name: DeepCORO-Integrated.
Summary.Training_run: Weights & Biases run 2563ce01 of project mhi_ai/deepcoro-segmentation: https://wandb.ai/mhi_ai/deepcoro-segmentation/runs/2563ce01

Mechanism.Outcome: Per-segment coronary stenosis, calcification, thrombus and chronic total occlusion (17 supported segments), study-level lesion probabilities, LAD FFR/iFR and coronary dominance
Mechanism.Output: model_version (v15); segments.<segment>.stenosis_pct (0-100, the model estimate), .display_pct (integer 0-100, the % shown in the report) and .display_category (normal, mild, moderate, intermediate, severe, occluded), .prob_significant (label: >= 70%, left main >= 50%), .prob_threshold, .significant (true when prob_significant > prob_threshold), .calcif_prob, .calcif, .thrombus_prob, .thrombus, .cto_prob, .cto (each flag true when its probability > the threshold of that finding); unsupported_segments (["lvp"]): segments.lvp keeps its numeric keys, has unsupported = true, its four flags are always false and it has no display_pct or display_category; lesion_thresholds.operating_point, .calcif, .thrombus, .cto; study_lesions.study_calcif_prob, .study_thrombus_prob, .study_cto_prob (probability that the finding is present in any segment; no yes/no call); lad_physiology.ffr, .ifr, .ffr_abnormal_prob (FFR <= 0.80), .ifr_abnormal_prob (iFR <= 0.89), .ffr_abnormal_threshold, .ifr_abnormal_threshold, .ffr_abnormal, .ifr_abnormal, .operating_point; model_dominance.dominance_left_prob (probability of a left-dominant circulation), .dominance_left_threshold, .dominance_left_pred (true when the probability > the threshold), .operating_point, .label_source; coronary_dominance (only when the caller sent additionalMetadata.coronaryDominance; it alone decides how the schema is drawn); n_videos, encoder_passes
Mechanism.Target_population: Adults undergoing diagnostic coronary angiography at MHI
Mechanism.Input_data_source: Diagnostic left and right coronary contrast runs (multi-frame XA DICOM)
Mechanism.Model_type: Deep learning: EchoJEPA ViT-L video encoder with its own segmentation decoder, tracked segment crops and per-segment attention pooling; stenosis and lesion (calcification, thrombus, CTO) heads on each segment; a study-level lesion reader over the full-view tokens; LAD physiology head on the left main / LAD / diagonal features; a coronary dominance head on the pooled segment features

Model.Purpose: Read stenosis severity and three lesion findings in every coronary segment and estimate LAD physiology from the angiogram alone
Model.Output: 18 stenosis percentages, probabilities and yes/no calls (17 supported; the posterior LV branch is unsupported); 18 x 3 lesion probabilities and yes/no flags; 3 study-level lesion probabilities; LAD FFR/iFR values, abnormal probabilities and yes/no calls; probability of a left-dominant circulation and its yes/no call

Uses_and_directions.General_use: Research preview of segment-level stenosis and lesion reading, image-only LAD physiology estimation and coronary dominance estimation.
Uses_and_directions.Target_population_and_use_case: Adults with diagnostic coronary angiography. Upload the diagnostic left and right coronary contrast runs (no PCI, stent or ventriculography runs); up to 12 are used, chosen by SeriesTime.
Uses_and_directions.Before_using_this_model: Held-out test (3,194 studies / 2,941 patients, read once; 95% patient-bootstrap confidence intervals): stenosis macro AUROC 0.877 over the 17 supported segments (model v13 0.883, DeepCORO-CLIP 0.846, EchoJEPA 0.848); mean per-segment Pearson r 0.508 (0.495-0.519), 8 of 17 segments above 0.5; mean ICC 0.438 (0.426-0.449). LAD FFR/iFR pooled AUROC 0.674 (0.605-0.737; 270 proximal or mid LAD measurements), FFR alone 0.71 (76), iFR alone 0.67 (194). Lesion findings, area under the precision-recall curve, mean over segments / all segments pooled: calcification 0.122 / 0.188, thrombus 0.402 / 0.321, CTO 0.139 / 0.160. Coronary dominance AUROC 0.923 (0.908-0.937; 2,943 studies, 203 left dominant) against labels derived from another model, not expert reads. Against model v13 on the same studies (paired differences v15 minus v13): stenosis is slightly lower (mean r -0.014, 95% CI -0.020 to -0.008; macro AUROC -0.006, -0.009 to -0.002), the pressure output is not distinguishable (-0.015, -0.059 to 0.030) and lesion detection is better (mean of the six lesion areas +0.034, 0.012 to 0.051; thrombus, mean over segments, +0.098, 0.025 to 0.159). Confirm every reading on the images.

Warnings_and_limitations.Input_selection: The model was trained only on diagnostic left/right coronary contrast runs without stents. This version does not filter uploads; PCI, stent, ventriculography or non-contrast runs will degrade the output.
Warnings_and_limitations.Distal_and_branch_segments: Agreement with the cath report is weaker for the posterolateral branch, distal LAD, distal LCx, diagonals, marginals and ramus (r 0.24-0.45 on test).
Warnings_and_limitations.Physiology: LAD FFR/iFR outputs reach AUROC 0.67 on test (0.674, 95% CI 0.605-0.737, 270 proximal or mid LAD measurements) and do not replace invasive measurement; FFR alone was tested on only 76 measurements. Model v13 reached 0.689 on the same measurements (v15 minus v13 -0.015, 95% CI -0.059 to 0.030: not distinguishable) and model v12 0.721 (v15 minus v12 -0.047, 95% CI -0.094 to -0.002). The pressure labels of v15 are proximal or mid LAD measurements only.
Warnings_and_limitations.Video_encoding: DICOMs are converted exactly as the training videos (MJPG AVI). About 13% of training/test videos had been stored as MP4; for those studies the DICOM path differs slightly from the AVI-based test results.
Warnings_and_limitations.Displayed_stenosis: The stenosis estimate is pulled toward the mean. The report shows a rescaled value (display calibration cal1 refitted on v15, data/stenosis_display.json): an estimate below 9.5% is shown as 0% (normal); above, the knots 9.5->20, 21.5->30, 34.5->50, 49.5->70 and 100->100 put the shown values on the angiographic categories <30, 30-49, 50-69 and >=70%; the interpolated value is rounded down, so the category boundaries are exactly at estimates of 21.5, 34.5 and 49.5. A CTO flag is shown as 100% and a segment flagged for significant stenosis is never shown as normal. Fitted on the validation split of the served v15 weights (4,647 studies, 78,999 segment readings of 17 segments; the posterior LV branch is not in the fit and is not displayed). Agreement with the report category on validation: 24% and weighted kappa 0.39 for the raw estimate; 64% and 0.58 for the mapping (65% and 0.58 in 5-fold patient cross-validation); 60% and 0.58 with the rule that a flagged segment is never shown as normal, which is what the report shows. 11.6% of the lesions reported at 70% or more are shown as normal by the mapping alone and 7.7% with that rule. The flags are unchanged and come from the probability, not from the shown %. The mapping of model v13 (below 10; 10->20, 23->30, 37->50, 51->70) is kept in data/stenosis_display_v13.json only to redraw stored v13 results and is not applied to v15.
Warnings_and_limitations.Confidence_Scores: Probabilities are not calibrated. The yes/no calls use thresholds chosen on the internal validation set, not validated clinical operating points; a call is positive when probability > threshold. Stenosis, pressure and dominance use the threshold with the highest geometric mean of sensitivity and specificity. On the held-out test set: FFR <= 0.80 at 0.5936: sensitivity 0.76, specificity 0.70 (76 measurements); iFR <= 0.89 at 0.6939: sensitivity 0.53, specificity 0.72 (194 measurements); significant stenosis, mean of the 17 supported segments: sensitivity 0.80, specificity 0.79, positive predictive value 0.26, negative predictive value 0.98. Left dominance at 0.0383 on the validation set (3,764 studies with a confident label, 228 left dominant): sensitivity 0.93, specificity 0.85, positive predictive value 0.29, negative predictive value 0.995; the release dossier gives no test operating point for dominance.
Warnings_and_limitations.Flags: Thresholds of rarely diseased segments are low (for example 0.0082 for distal LCx), so a segment can be flagged with a low probability and a low estimated percentage. At least one segment is flagged for stenosis in 41% of test studies without any significant lesion in the report and in 97% of those with one (dossier figures, computed with the posterior LV branch flag, which this container never raises). FFR and iFR are separate outputs and their calls can disagree in the same study.
Warnings_and_limitations.Lesion_flags: Calcification, thrombus and CTO are rare (1.9%, 0.2% and 0.7% of segment readings in the test set), so their flags use one threshold per finding set for 99% specificity on the validation set. On the held-out test set (57,492 segment readings): calcification at 0.3631: sensitivity 0.19, specificity 0.9895, positive predictive value 0.27; CTO at 0.2134: sensitivity 0.35, specificity 0.990, positive predictive value 0.19; thrombus at 0.0648 (the 99% specificity point, not the one in use): sensitivity 0.55, specificity 0.992, positive predictive value 0.11. The thrombus flag uses the fixed threshold 0.40 instead (kept from 1.4.1). On the v15 validation set (83,646 segment readings, 200 with thrombus in the report) 0.40 flags 166 segments, 43 of them with thrombus (positive predictive value 0.26, sensitivity 0.215), against 912 flagged, 79 true, positive predictive value 0.087 and sensitivity 0.395 at 0.0648. The 0.40 threshold has not been evaluated on the test set. Most findings are missed and most flags are false: an absent flag does not exclude the finding. Lesion labels come from the angiography report.
Warnings_and_limitations.Study_level_lesions: study_lesions gives one probability per finding for the whole study (any segment). It has no threshold and no yes/no call, and the release dossier reports no performance figure for it: treat it as an uncalibrated score.
Warnings_and_limitations.Dominance: model_dominance is the model's own estimate of a left-dominant circulation. Its training and evaluation labels were derived from another model (majority over the right coronary videos), not read by experts, and it is less reliable in studies without a right coronary run. It is reported as text and does not change the schema: the schema follows the caller-supplied coronary_dominance (angiogram classifier majority) when present and is drawn right dominant otherwise.
Warnings_and_limitations.Unsupported_outputs: The posterior left ventricular branch (lvp) had no training target in model v15. Its keys stay in the JSON for compatibility; the numbers are not meaningful, its flags are always false, it has no display fields and it is never shown in the report, the diagnosis or the explanations. The post-PCI outputs of model v15 (stent, final TIMI flow, failed PCI) need post-PCI runs as input and are not produced by this container.
Warnings_and_limitations.Comparison_with_v13: Model v15 replaces v13 with a slightly lower stenosis agreement (mean r 0.508 against 0.521; paired difference -0.014, 95% CI -0.020 to -0.008; ICC 0.438 against 0.461; macro AUROC 0.877 against 0.883, paired -0.006, -0.009 to -0.002), a pressure output that is not distinguishable (0.674 against 0.689) and better lesion detection (thrombus area under the precision-recall curve 0.402 against 0.304). The per-model confidence intervals of r overlap. Results stored by versions 1.1.0 to 1.4.1 are v13 results: they are redrawn with their own stored display values (or the v13 mapping) and headed v13-cal1.

Changelogs.2.0.0: 2026-11-15: Numbered 2.0.0 because new weights are a major version under the release policy. The PyTorch build of this image is not the one the test metrics were computed with: it is numerically close to the evaluated model, not identical. On 300 validation studies accuracy is equal (17-segment mean correlation 0.4933 against 0.4932); an individual stenosis estimate differs by 0.25 points in median, 2.9 at the 95th percentile and rarely much more (49 at most), and some yes/no calls differ. The test-set metrics were not recomputed with this build. The image installs PyTorch 2.11.0 built for CUDA 12.8 instead of 2.14.1 built for CUDA 13.0, which could not use the GPUs of a server with an NVIDIA 570 driver. Serves model v15 (Weights & Biases run 2563ce01, Hugging Face revision ab6d12f, tag v15.1) with its own thresholds. New in the JSON, no existing key changed: model_version, study_lesions (study_calcif_prob, study_thrombus_prob, study_cto_prob; probability only), model_dominance (dominance_left_prob, dominance_left_threshold 0.0383, dominance_left_pred), unsupported_segments. The posterior LV branch (lvp) has no training target in v15: its keys stay, its flags are always false, it has unsupported = true and no display fields. Display calibration cal1 refitted on the v15 validation split (below 9.5 -> normal; 9.5->20, 21.5->30, 34.5->50, 49.5->70, 100->100; rounded down); the report header reads v15-cal1. /inference/render-report draws a stored result with the display values, calibration note, performance figures and header of its own model version: a v13 result (1.1.0 to 1.4.1) is never given the v15 mapping. The thrombus flag keeps the fixed threshold 0.40 (v15 validation: 166 segments flagged, 43 with thrombus, PPV 0.26, sensitivity 0.215; not evaluated on the test set). The caller-supplied coronaryDominance is unchanged and still decides the schema; the model's own dominance is shown as text. Test set against v13: stenosis slightly lower (mean r 0.508 against 0.521), pressure not distinguishable (0.674 against 0.689), lesion detection better (thrombus AUPRC 0.402 against 0.304).
Changelogs.1.4.1: 2026-11-15: Same model (v13) and weights. The thrombus flag now needs a probability above 0.40 instead of 0.0851 (Thresholds.lesion_threshold_overrides in models/config.json; returned operating point: specificity_99 (thrombus: fixed 0.40)). Chosen on the validation split of the served weights (4,647 studies, 200 segments with thrombus in the report) to raise the positive predictive value: at 0.40, 60 segments are flagged, 18 of them with thrombus in the report (PPV 0.30, sensitivity 0.09), against 902 flagged, PPV 0.08 and sensitivity 0.36 at 0.0851. No threshold reaches a PPV of 0.80 on more than one segment. Not evaluated on the test set. thrombus_prob is unchanged; results stored by earlier versions keep the flags they were computed with. Calcification and CTO thresholds are unchanged.
Changelogs.1.4.0: 2026-11-14: Same model (v13), weights and thresholds; stenosis_pct and every flag unchanged. Display calibration cal1 of the stenosis estimate: each segment gets display_pct and display_category, and the report (schema labels, segment detail, summary and diagnosis text) shows display_pct, with 0% worded as normal (estimate below 10%). A segment flagged for significant stenosis is never shown as normal. The report header reads v13-cal1 (reportModelVersion). The mapping (below 10% -> 0%; 10->20, 23->30, 37->50, 51->70, 100->100) was fitted on the validation split of the served v13 weights, without the posterior LV branch rows (weak report grading); it is applied to every displayed segment. Schema drawing of the lesion flags (drawing only): a calcified segment lies on a grey band with calcium plates, the vessel distal to a CTO flag is drawn grey (no antegrade flow shown), and a thrombus flag is drawn as a clot symbol in the lumen.
Changelogs.1.3.0: 2026-11-13: Same model (v13), weights, thresholds and report. POST /inference/render-report draws the HTML report of a stored JSON-mode result (identical to HTML-mode predict for the same prediction) on the CPU without loading the model; model-info advertises capabilities.renderReport. predictions.explainability[i].images (crop and frame, base64 JPEG) is now kept in the JSON so a stored result renders with its pictures.
Changelogs.1.2.0: 2026-11-13: Same model (v13), weights and thresholds. The HTML report draws the 18 segments on a coronary schema instead of a table. An optional additionalMetadata.coronaryDominance (study majority of the angiogram procedure classifier over the diagnostic videos sent) is validated, returned as predictions.coronary_dominance, added to the diagnosis and used to draw the schema left or right dominant. In the report and diagnosis a CTO-flagged segment is shown as occluded at 100% (stenosis estimate kept in the JSON), thrombus flags are drawn as a filling defect, and the posterior LV branch is not shown (still in the JSON). For each flagged stenosis segment (up to 6) the report shows the tracked crop with the highest attention, the within-crop attention the model applied (recomputed exactly from the same forward call) and the full frame with the crop box; the JSON gets the matching metadata in predictions.explainability without images.
Changelogs.1.1.2: 2026-11-12: Same model (v13), same thresholds and same code. The image now installs PyTorch 2.14.1 built for CUDA 13.0 instead of 2.5.1 built for CUDA 12.1, so it also runs on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. Returned numbers differ slightly from those of the development environment in which the test metrics were computed (44 of 8,880 yes/no calls on 120 test studies; same AUROC to 2 decimals); see the README.
Changelogs.1.1.1: 2026-11-12: Same model (v13). Probabilities are returned with 6 decimals instead of 4 and every yes/no call is taken on the returned probability, so a response never shows a probability at its threshold next to a positive call.
Changelogs.1.1.0: 2026-11-12: Serves model v13 (Weights & Biases run 400d0a77): adds calcification, thrombus and CTO probabilities and flags per segment and the Thresholds key lesion_operating_point. Stenosis is unchanged on test (macro AUROC 0.885 against 0.884); pressure AUROC is 0.69 against 0.72 for v12.
Changelogs.1.0.0: 2026-11-12: Serves model v12: 18-segment stenosis and LAD FFR/iFR with validation-derived thresholds.
